gen-tourney-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Wide-stretched letters cut at a single stroke width give Tourney its locker-room punch, while Pilcrow Rounded tucks its letters tight beneath. The sturdy-meets-soft mix is what makes this pairing memorable.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-supreme: Quilon swells and thins its strokes with quiet modesty, while Supreme lays a dense, heavy-looking strip of text below. Editorial polish up top, crisp weight underneath: that is the strength here.
gen-fs-quilon-manrope: Manrope holds a constant, wire-bent line width, while the headings in Quilon swell and thin with mild, approachable contrast. Long paragraphs would glide, each curve showing a bright gap.
gen-fs-quilon-satoshi: Satoshi draws every stroke with one marker tip and stands tall on a soaring x-height, while Quilon lightly modulates its headings. Long lines of it stay open and unhurried, never squeezing shut.
gen-fs-quilon-work-sans: Work Sans keeps one stroke width across the whole alphabet. Work Sans is the steady worker, while Quilon thins its bowls gracefully and carries the commanding editorial voice.
gen-megrim-fs-hind: Angular and futuristic, Megrim shoots up on a skyward x-height line with an open, paperclip-bent c. But Hind does its best work in drawn-string strokes and lowercase nearly matching its capitals.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded tucks its letters close and leaves curves open, while Mystery Quest brings bookish, nostalgic open-jawed curves. Little modulation in either keeps the two moving in step.
gen-almendra-display-inter: Ornate, literary flair: Almendra Display keeps its letters from pinching shut and lifts a pronounced x-height. And Inter runs smooth and tube-like, its counters breathing through paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-fs-quicksan: Loud, level and bold: Love Ya Like A Sister barely lifts its ascenders. Quicksand brings blown-glass bowls and uniform bar thickness, and that soft consistency is the pairing's real strength.
gen-fs-styro-fs-public-sans: Public Sans spreads broad, open counters across a hefty lowercase, while Styro packs its letters tight with barely a gap. Closed against open is the whole story, and it's a retro-meets-trustworthy one.
